claims.text: The initial material is a homogeneous, single-phase high-entropy-alloy solid solution.
The initial alloy contains low levels of interstitial oxygen and nitrogen.
High mechanical stress accelerates local segregation of trace interstitial impurities.
Segregated interstitial impurities nucleate nanoscale brittle secondary phases at dislocation networks and grain boundaries.
The governing behavior can be tested by comparing mechanically loaded samples in oxygen-containing and inert atmospheres.
An inert testing atmosphere minimizes the relevant impurity exposure relative to an atmosphere containing trace oxygen.
Impurity diffusion sufficient to cause degradation can occur from ambient to moderately elevated temperatures under the proposed service conditions.
Mechanical loading promotes local diffusion and segregation of impurity atoms.
Interstitial-impurity segregation destabilizes the ductile solid solution and induces phase segregation or transformation into brittle ordered regions.
The resulting brittle regions act as crack initiators and reduce fracture toughness.
Loaded samples will have lower fracture toughness than the initial homogeneous baseline.
Loaded samples will have lower elongation to failure than the initial homogeneous baseline.
TEM or SEM will reveal impurity-induced secondary phases along dislocation channels and grain boundaries after loading.
As-cast and annealed high-entropy alloys with uniform single-phase microstructures provide a high-toughness, high-ductility baseline.
Degradation is favored by higher stress amplitudes, prolonged loading, and oxygen-containing environments.
Minimizing impurity levels or loading in an inert atmosphere should preserve toughness.
The effects and segregation kinetics of individual impurity species may vary with alloy composition and processing history.

Similar toughness reductions and phase evolution in high- and low-impurity controls, or toughness loss without detectable secondary phases, would falsify the proposed impurity-induced phase-segregation mechanism.
